name: Barbell Front Squat
summary: A squat variation with the bar held on the front of the shoulders, which keeps the torso upright and puts a strong emphasis on the quads and trunk. It also demands good upper-back strength and mobility.
setup: Set the bar in a rack at about mid-chest height.
Step up to the bar and rest it on the front of your shoulders, close to your throat but not pressing on it, using a clean grip or crossed-arm grip.
Lift your elbows so your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, then unrack and step back.
Set your feet about shoulder width with toes turned out slightly and brace your trunk.
execution: Take a breath, brace, and sit straight down while your knees track forward over your toes.
Keep your elbows high so the bar stays on your shoulders and your chest stays tall.
Lower to at least thigh parallel, or as deep as you can control without your torso collapsing.
Drive up through the whole foot, keeping the elbows up the entire time.
Re-rack once the set is done by walking forward until the bar touches the hooks.
cues: Sit straight down between the hips
mistakes: Elbows dropping and the torso folding forward: lighten the load, lift the elbows and think about pushing the chest up.
Bar rolling off the shoulders because of a poor grip: use the crossed-arm grip or work on wrist and lat mobility, or switch to straps for a bodybuilder-style hold.
Heels lifting: widen the stance a little, or wear flat shoes with a firm sole.
Rounding the upper back at the bottom: reduce depth and the weight until you can hold position.
